_note: Governed Script Factory vocabulary and executable forge state for Zo bootstrap deployments.

auto-chunker.meaning: Detects risky or oversized requests and splits them into bounded work chunks.
auto-chunker.rule: Use auto-chunker before risky build or transport work.

cell-bootstrap.meaning: Initializes a Zo cell or hive node from the portable bootstrap package.
cell-bootstrap.rule: Use cell-bootstrap for install, verify, and init flows.

intake-engine.meaning: Routes prompts through known scripts or records a script gap.
intake-engine.rule: Use intake-engine before ad hoc implementation.

decompress.meaning: Expands compressed or encoded factory packets back into readable contract content.
decompress.rule: Use decompress when machine transport must be inspected or restored to human-readable form.

emit-contract.meaning: Creates a structured contract packet from a bounded prompt or factory request.
emit-contract.rule: Use emit-contract before transport or worker execution when a durable typed packet is needed.

dataset-store.meaning: Writes local dataset rows for contracts, logs, registry, and talkback surfaces.
dataset-store.rule: Use dataset-store when a script needs a durable local record.

forge-auto-capture.meaning: Watches for missing script patterns and seeds durable script-gap or capture records.
forge-auto-capture.rule: Use forge-auto-capture to turn repeated missing-script needs into governed follow-up work.

factory-cli.meaning: Command entry point that routes list, scan, heartbeat, registry, doctor, and prompt intake.
factory-cli.rule: Use factory-cli for repeatable local factory commands.

heartbeat.meaning: Periodic train runner that loads train-cars and adapts the next pulse interval.
heartbeat.rule: Heartbeat owns the tick loop; train cars own bounded tick work.

hive-api.meaning: Hive distribution route that serves manifest, node records, registration, heartbeat, and ack responses.
hive-api.rule: Use hive-api on the hive distribution node.

hive-dispatcher.meaning: Builds bootstrap packages and records package dispatch state for downstream nodes.
hive-dispatcher.rule: Use hive-dispatcher to package hive or cell bundles.

hive-receive.meaning: Hive endpoint handler for registration, status, and bounded dispatch payloads.
hive-receive.rule: Use hive-receive on deployed hive endpoint surfaces.

talkback.meaning: Reports node status and handles compact hive query responses.
talkback.rule: Use talkback for node health, status, and result evidence.

scan-workspace.meaning: Scans bounded non-secret workspace surfaces and writes a scan artifact.
scan-workspace.rule: Use scan-workspace to refresh local context without reading secrets.

page-add.meaning: Creates a page artifact with standard IMSCE page/index and page-modal structure.
page-add.rule: Use page-add when a request needs a new route or page artifact.

section-add.meaning: Creates a section artifact that sits inside a page modal and accepts cards.
section-add.rule: Use section-add for page sections such as hero, content, or footer.

card-add.meaning: Creates a card artifact with slots for title, body, and actions.
card-add.rule: Use card-add for bounded widgets or grouped content inside a section.

button-add.meaning: Creates a button element artifact with anchored placement.
button-add.rule: Use button-add when a card or form needs a governed button element.

field-add.meaning: Creates a form field element artifact.
field-add.rule: Use field-add for input fields inside governed form artifacts.

text-add.meaning: Creates a text, label, or heading element artifact.
text-add.rule: Use text-add for governed copy, labels, or headings.

form-add.meaning: Creates a form artifact with field definitions and a submit button.
form-add.rule: Use form-add when a page or card needs a governed form structure.

git-commit.meaning: Reserved source-control forge for commit/push work.
git-commit.rule: Keep blocked for autonomous Zo execution; source-control mutation requires explicit human control.

deploy-pages.meaning: Reserved deployment forge for publishing page artifacts.
deploy-pages.rule: Keep blocked for autonomous Zo execution; deployment requires explicit human control.

atomic-common.meaning: Shared helper module used by atomic artifact forges for argument parsing, workspace scanning, labels, routes, and artifact writes.
atomic-common.rule: Categorize as a utility helper, not a runnable forge. It supports artifact forges and should not appear as a user-facing script.

heartbeat-car.meaning: Train car that refreshes dashboard state and optionally pings hive status.
heartbeat-car.rule: Runs first on every heartbeat tick.

spawn-worker-car.meaning: Train car that runs one bounded local inbox worker when pending tandem contracts exist.
spawn-worker-car.rule: Never runs arbitrary commands; it routes through contract-inbox-runner.

scan-workspace-car.meaning: Train car that refreshes the bounded workspace scan when the latest scan is stale.
scan-workspace-car.rule: Uses scan-workspace rather than broad ad hoc filesystem reads.

hive-sync-car.meaning: Train car that checks a configured hive manifest and records update availability.
hive-sync-car.rule: Reports sync state only; package application remains governed by explicit scripts.

route-manifest-bridge.meaning: Applies route injection manifests to Zo Space routes through a repeatable MCP bridge.
route-manifest-bridge.rule: The bridge is generic. App-specific manifest generators must stay in app scope, not in the generic factory runtime.

interlink.meaning: Provides Zo-to-Zo or factory-to-factory interlink transport helpers for emergency or directed coordination.
interlink.rule: Use interlink only for bounded cross-node transport; prefer file/API tandem when possible.

script-dictionary.meaning: Generates or refreshes dictionary-style script terminology artifacts from local factory definitions.
script-dictionary.rule: Use script-dictionary to keep Scriptionary vocabulary inspectable and local-first.

Scriptonomy.DISCUSS: Free-form AI chat; bypasses scripts unless a governed route exists.
Scriptonomy.MICRO: Single bounded mutation or local operation.
Scriptonomy.BUILD: Full scoped work; requires enough typed context to execute.
Scriptonomy.PLAN: Novel or complex request routed to planning before execution.

BootstrapSources.github: Clone from the canonical repo when a full bootstrap is needed.
BootstrapSources.hive: Pull packages from a registered hive endpoint.
BootstrapSources.interlink: Zo-to-Zo API lane for emergency or directed transfer.
BootstrapSources.skill: Use the refer-library-bootstrap skill where installed.

HiveCellArchitecture.Hive: Distribution hub that owns manifest, receives heartbeats, and dispatches work.
HiveCellArchitecture.Cell: Registered Zo node that runs scripts and reports talkback.
HiveCellArchitecture.Terminal: Standalone Zo node not yet connected to a hive.

ExecutionSequence.definition: Canonical rank order for how factory rules, intake, resolvers, references, scripts, runs, evidence, repairs, and promotion are applied.
ExecutionSequence.rule: Use SEQ-A through SEQ-L to decide hierarchy before choosing a script route. Lower ranks execute before higher ranks when both apply. Use dotted sub-sequences inside parent ranks.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-A: Kernel Governance: always-on Script Factory and Smart Intake rules.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-B: Request Intake: prompt, document, command, or API request becomes a compact contract.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-C: Clarification Resolver: ambiguity is reduced with bounded choices or a deterministic route.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-D: Authority And Context: official references, local context, active rule packs, and user method scope are gathered.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-E: Strategy Selection: sequencer chooses the named strategy, method, forge, and script route.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-F: Forge Or Script Generation: missing deterministic behavior is generated or modified as a candidate.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-G: Script Execution: selected registered script or candidate runs against the contract.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-H: Evidence Capture: observed effect, changed artifacts, checks, receipts, and talkback are recorded.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-I: Effect Comparison: observed effect is compared with intended effect and allowed boundary.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-J: Modification Loop: mismatches repair the smallest responsible layer and rerun the same contract.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-K: Promotion And Registration: verified scripts, methods, strategies, or rule packs become active in scope.
ExecutionSequence.SEQ-L: Scriptionary Refresh: new terms, sequence changes, methods, strategies, and artifacts are written back to the text map blueprint.

SubSequences.definition: Nested deterministic ranks inside a parent execution sequence layer.
SubSequences.rule: Use sub-sequences when a main sequence step needs deterministic internal branching, checks, repair, or replay without creating a new top-level rank.
SubSequences.SEQ-E.1: Condition Read: read contract, registry, active rule packs, locks, and evidence.
SubSequences.SEQ-E.2: Chain Decision: choose continue, branch, fork, merge, modify, delete, skip, block, supersede, or promote.
SubSequences.SEQ-E.3: Collision Check: compare read, write, and lock surfaces before allowing parallel branches.
SubSequences.SEQ-J.1: Mismatch Classifier: classify the mismatch and choose the smallest responsible repair layer.
SubSequences.SEQ-J.2: Repair Action: modify, delete, replace, regenerate, or block the affected script chain element.
SubSequences.SEQ-J.3: Replay Gate: rerun the same contract after repair and compare observed effect again.

ConditionalChainController.definition: Deterministic layer that manages chain continuation, splits, forks, merges, modification, deletion, skips, blocks, supersession, and promotion.
ConditionalChainController.rule: Every action must record condition, chosen action, affected scripts, surfaces, and evidence. Forks require non-colliding surfaces. Deletes require reason, archive or rollback path, and registry update.

NamedPatterns.Method Name: Stable name for a repeatable way a user, project, domain, forge, or factory prefers to perform work.
NamedPatterns.Strategy Name: Stable name for a reusable plan that coordinates methods, scripts, sequence ranks, and checks to reach an intended effect.
NamedPatterns.Text Map Blueprint: A scriptionary and legend detailed enough to reconstruct terms, hierarchy, sequence, methods, strategies, and activation rules from text.
NamedPatterns.rule: Methods and strategies must declare activation trigger, sequence ranks, intended effect, scope, and evidence path before registration.

NaturalRuleIntake.meaning: Users upload documents, state preferences, correct outputs, or give rules in ordinary language.
NaturalRuleIntake.rule: Do not ask users to label laws as unscripted or dormant. Smart Intake captures natural rule input and routes it to doctrine compilation, categorization, fixtures, modification loop, and registry promotion.

Clarifications.scan-workspace: The executable scanner is artifacts/scan-workspace.mjs. The train-car entry train-cars/03-scan-workspace.mjs is a heartbeat wrapper that calls the scanner when stale. A root scripts/factory/scan-workspace.mjs file is not canonical in this source tree; if a deployed node reports one, treat it as stale deployment drift unless it is deliberately reintroduced and registered.
Clarifications.artifacts-directory: The source artifact forges live in scripts/factory/artifacts/. If a deployed node reports artifacts/ as empty, resync the artifact forge files from source before treating the node as complete.
